description: For every integer k ≥ 6 with k ≡ 2 (mod 4), and for every pair of nonnegative integers (a, b) with a + b = k and a ≥ 1, the number 2^a · 3^b − 1 is composite. This formalizes the paper's theorem that row k of the principal skeleton L₁ contains no primes when k ≡ 2 (mod 4) and k ≥ 6. The proof exploits that k even forces a and b to share parity. When both even, 2^a · 3^b − 1 = (2^{a/2} · 3^{b/2} − 1)(2^{a/2} · 3^{b/2} + 1) via difference of squares, with both factors > 1 for k ≥ 6. When both odd, k ≡ 2 (mod 4) forces a ≡ b (mod 4), yielding 2^a · 3^b ≡ 1 (mod 5) so 5 | (2^a · 3^b − 1), and the cofactor exceeds 1 since k ≥ 6 excludes the case a = b = 1 where the value equals 5.
proof_strategy: Case split on parity of a and b. Since k ≡ 2 (mod 4) is even, a and b have the same parity. Case 1 (both even): apply difference of squares factorization 2^a · 3^b − 1 = (2^{a/2} · 3^{b/2} − 1)(2^{a/2} · 3^{b/2} + 1), verify both factors exceed 1 using k ≥ 6. Case 2 (both odd): from a + b ≡ 2 (mod 4) with a,b odd, deduce a ≡ b (mod 4); compute 2^a · 3^b mod 5 using 2^4 ≡ 3^4 ≡ 1 (mod 5) to show 5 | (2^a · 3^b − 1); verify 2^a · 3^b − 1 > 5 since k ≥ 6 excludes (a,b) = (1,1). Subsume b = 0 into Case 1 since then a = k is even.
title: No primes in rows k ≡ 2 (mod 4) of the principal Collatz skeleton L₁

description: For each n ≥ 1, the map φ_n from the degree-n graded piece of the cone algebra on ℚⁿ to the (n−1)-chains of the ind-triangulation of S^{n−1} at all rational rays, defined on linearly independent tuples (v₁,…,vₙ) by φ_n([C(v₁,…,vₙ)]) = sgn(det(v₁,…,vₙ)) · Δ(ℚv₁,…,ℚvₙ), extends to a GL_n(ℚ)-equivariant isomorphism of ℚ-modules. This identifies the top-degree cone algebra graded piece with the spherical chain module computing H_{n−1}(S^{n−1}; ℚ).
proof_strategy: Define the cone algebra with its degree filtration and construct the spherical chain complex C(n) from rational rays with the stellar subdivision presentation. Verify well-definedness of φ_n by checking it respects the relations on both sides (stellar subdivision on the chain side, additivity on the cone side). Prove equivariance by direct computation of the GL_n(ℚ)-action on both sides. Establish bijectivity by constructing an explicit inverse using the presentation of C(n)_{n-1} and the identification of simplicial cones with oriented intersections of half-spaces.
title: GL_n-equivariant isomorphism between graded cone algebra and spherical chains

description: The transformation matrix encoding the change of the h-vector of a simplicial complex under the r-colored barycentric subdivision is totally positive (all minors are non-negative). The paper establishes that this matrix is TP_2, and this conjecture posits that the stronger total positivity (TP) property holds, extending the confirmed TP property of the standard barycentric and interval subdivisions.
proof_strategy: Extend the combinatorial network representation or the sufficient conditions for total positivity used for the barycentric and interval subdivisions to the r-colored barycentric subdivision. This may involve verifying the Whitney conditions or finding a suitable planar network whose path-generating function equals the transformation matrix entries.
title: Total positivity of the r-colored barycentric subdivision transformation matrix

description: For an odd prime p, let n = (p-1)/2 and χ be the Legendre symbol modulo p. For a ∈ F_p^×, define D_a(0) = det_{1 ≤ i,j ≤ n}(χ(i^2 - a*j)). Then D_a(0) = 0 if and only if p ≡ 3 (mod 4) and χ(a * n!) = 1.
proof_strategy: Define the Legendre symbol and the matrix M over the integers. Show that the determinant of M vanishes under the stated conditions by applying row and column operations to relate the determinant to the Pfaffian of an associated skew-symmetric matrix, leveraging properties of quadratic residues modulo p.
title: Vanishing Criterion for Legendre Symbol Determinants

description: For any connected trivalent ribbon graph G embedded on a closed surface, the degree-zero Penrose homology group H^{0,*}(G) at the specialization λ = 3 is nonzero if and only if G admits a proper 3-edge coloring (Tait coloring). This refines the classical Penrose criterion—which states P(G;3) > 0 iff G is Tait-colorable—by identifying the specific homological degree that detects colorability, analogous to how Khovanov homology detects the unknot in degree zero.
proof_strategy: Forward direction: For each Tait coloring c of G, construct an explicit generator of H^{0,*}(G) using the state-sum structure of the Penrose homology cube of resolutions, ensuring distinct colorings yield linearly independent classes. Reverse direction: Show that any nonzero class in H^{0,*}(G) forces the existence of a Tait coloring by analyzing the cobordism maps in the TQFT-valued chain complex and proving that non-colorable graphs have vanishing H^{0,*}. The nonorientable cobordism framework is essential for handling the sign assignments that distinguish colorable from non-colorable configurations.
title: Penrose Homology Detects Tait Colorability

description: For every connected simple graph G of order at least three, the independence number α(G) is bounded below by the sum of the annihilation number a(G) and the Havel-Hakimi residue res(G), divided by the maximum degree Δ(G). That is, α(G) ≥ (a(G) + res(G)) / Δ(G), or equivalently, α(G) * Δ(G) ≥ a(G) + res(G).
proof_strategy: Formalize the annihilation number, Havel-Hakimi residue, and maximum degree for simple graphs. Construct annihilating decompositions and prove the edge count inequality e(A) ≤ e(B) for the partition. Combine this with the classical Havel-Hakimi residue inequality res(G) ≤ α(G) and the Caro-Wei bounds to establish the multiplicative inequality.
title: TxGraffiti Annihilation-Residue Inequality

description: For all positive integers m and n, the number of intervals in the greedy m-Tamari poset on m-Dyck paths of semi-length n equals the number of rooted planar (m+1)-constellations with n black faces. This generalizes the m=1 case proven in the paper (where greedy Tamari intervals are equinumerous to bipartite planar maps, i.e., 2-constellations) and remains open for m ≥ 2.
proof_strategy: The m=1 proof establishes a recursive decomposition isomorphism between greedy Tamari intervals and bipartite planar maps. For general m, one would need to: (1) formalize m-Dyck paths and the greedy m-Tamari poset cover relation; (2) define planar (m+1)-constellations; (3) establish that both families satisfy isomorphic recursive decomposition schemes; (4) conclude equinumerosity by induction. The refined conjecture additionally tracks the number of vertices of degree m+1 in the constellation and the number of ascents of the lower bound of the interval.
title: Equinumerosity of greedy m-Tamari intervals and planar (m+1)-constellations

description: For any real t ≥ 3, the absolute value of the Riemann zeta function on the 1-line is bounded by 1/2 log t + 1.57. This formalizes the primary improved 'trivial' bound from the paper using smoothing techniques, bypassing the need for exponential sum arguments for smaller values of t.
proof_strategy: Formalize the smooth approximation of zeta(1+it) using the exponential sum with the kernel exp(-n/X). Decompose the sum, bound the error terms using bounds on |zeta(1/2+it)|, and optimize the parameter X to derive the explicit constant 1.57.
title: Explicit Upper Bound on the Riemann Zeta Function on the 1-Line via Smoothing

description: Conjectures that the set of indices n for which the coefficients V_2(n) of the q-series v_2(q) = sum_{n>=1} q^{2n^2-n} / (-q; q^2)_n violate the alternating sign pattern (-1)^{n+1} V_2(n) > 0 is finite. The paper proves that this set has natural density zero using an adapted circle method, but finiteness remains open and requires effective bounds on the asymptotic error terms.
proof_strategy: Obtain effective explicit bounds for the error terms in the asymptotic formulas for V_2(n) derived via the circle method, demonstrating that the main term strictly dominates the error term for all sufficiently large n, thereby forcing the strict alternating sign pattern eventually.
title: Finiteness of Sign Exceptions for Andrews' q-Series v_2

description: For any prime p, the Markov chain on ℕ defined by the Klagsbrun-Mazur-Rubin twist process for p-Selmer ranks of even-dimensional Galois modules satisfying the KMR technical conditions is irreducible, aperiodic, and positive recurrent. Its unique stationary distribution π assigns strictly positive probability to every rank r ∈ ℕ, and the distribution of p-Selmer ranks in the twist family ordered by the product of ramified primes converges to π.
proof_strategy: 1) Define the KMR Markov chain as an explicit stochastic kernel on ℕ capturing the effect of local twist conditions on p-Selmer ranks. 2) Prove irreducibility by constructing explicit paths from any state to any other via sequences of local twist operations. 3) Prove aperiodicity by exhibiting positive self-loop probability at state 0. 4) Establish positive recurrence via drift analysis or Lyapunov function arguments on the countable state space. 5) Apply the convergence theorem for irreducible aperiodic positive recurrent chains to deduce convergence to the unique stationary distribution. 6) Positivity of π follows from irreducibility.
title: KMR Markov chain convergence and positivity of p-Selmer rank stationary distribution

description: For any d-dimensional spanning k-tree K contained in the join V₁*⋯*V_{d+1} and any affine map A:|Δ_V|→ℝ^d with 0∈A(V_i) for all i, there exists a face σ∈K with 0∈A(σ) such that the number of faces in K is bounded by a polynomial in |V| of degree at most k+1. Moreover, when k=1 (spanning trees), the bound is linear in |V|.
proof_strategy: Construct explicit minimal subcomplexes using induction on k, leveraging the recursive structure of spanning k-trees where each k-tree can be built from a (k-1)-tree by adding a spanning tree structure. Apply the known result for k=0 (bipartite case) recursively while maintaining the polynomial bound through careful counting of faces in the iterated join construction.
title: Colorful Carathéodory theorem for spanning k-trees admits a polynomial-size witness

description: The paper proves an edge-spectral supersaturation bound with a sharp constant $B_F$ for color-critical graphs $F$ with $\chi(F) \ge 4$. A natural open problem is whether the same bound holds for $\chi(F) = 3$, most notably for triangles ($K_3$). The conjecture states that for every $\epsilon > 0$, there exist $\delta > 0$ and $M$ such that for all $m \ge M$ and $0 < q \le \delta \sqrt{m}$, any graph $G$ with $m$ edges and $\lambda^2(G) \ge m + q$ contains at least $(1 - \epsilon) q \sqrt{m}$ triangles, corresponding to the sharp constant $B_{K_3} = 1$.
proof_strategy: Adapt the spectral stability methods used for $\chi(F) \ge 4$ to the $\chi(F)=3$ case. This requires establishing spectral stability for near-bipartite graphs, then applying supersaturation counting arguments within the bipartite structure to find the requisite number of triangles. The bipartite case $r=2$ might require different spectral inequalities or combinatorial reductions since the Li-Liu-Zhang bound was only for $r \ge 3$.
title: Edge-Spectral Supersaturation for Triangles

description: The generalized honeymoon Oberwolfach problem HOP(2^{⟨s⟩}, 2m), which seats 2n participants (with n = s + m) at s tables of size 2 and one round table of size 2m such that each participant sits next to their spouse every time and next to each other participant exactly once, has a solution if and only if s > 0 or m is even.
proof_strategy: Formalize the necessary graph-theoretic definitions for 4-fold graphs and HOP decompositions. Prove the equivalence between the seating problem and the graph decomposition problem (Theorem 3.2). Establish base cases by formalizing Lemma 3.3 (for odd m) and Lemma 3.4 (for even m). Construct the general solution by inductively building decompositions for larger n by extending the graph using 1-regular subgraph decompositions (Lemma 3.5 and Lemma 3.6).
title: Complete Solution to the Generalized Honeymoon Oberwolfach Problem with One Round Table

description: For every finite poset P of width at most 2, the Ehrhart h*-polynomial h*(O(P); t) of the order polytope O(P) is real-rooted. This extends the paper's result for generalized snake posets (a proper subclass of width-two posets) to all width-two posets, and would unify real-rootedness phenomena observed across flow polytopes, rook polynomials, and P-Eulerian polynomials for this entire width regime.
proof_strategy: Decompose an arbitrary width-two poset into a union of chains and analyze how its Jordan-Hölder set and P-Eulerian polynomial relate to a generalized non-nesting rook polynomial on an associated Ferrers diagram. The key obstacle is that arbitrary width-two posets need not be generalized snake posets, so the existing rook polynomial correspondence must be extended to handle arbitrary interleavings of two chains, possibly via interlacing root arguments or real-rootedness-preserving operations on the associated generating polynomials.
title: Real-rootedness of h*-polynomials for width-two order polytopes

description: The paper establishes the upper bound $f_{F,G}(n) \le C(\log n)^{\beta_F}$ for $r$-uniform hypergraphs. This conjecture proposes that this bound is asymptotically tight, meaning there exists a constant $c > 0$ such that $f_{F,G}(n) \ge c(\log n)^{\beta_F}$ for any non-empty $r$-graph $F$ and $2$-tightly connected $r$-graph $G$ with no homomorphism from $G$ to $F$, thereby completely determining the polylogarithmic exponent $\beta_F$.
proof_strategy: Construct $G$-free hypergraphs using probabilistic methods, such as the random greedy algorithm or altered random structures, and analyze their induced $F$-free subgraphs. The analysis would require establishing isoperimetric inequalities on the 2-shadow $\partial_2F$ to demonstrate that any large enough induced subgraph must contain a copy of $F$, yielding the matching lower bound.
title: Matching Lower Bound for Generalized Erdős–Rogers Functions

description: For integers n, k, t with n >= 3 and 0 <= k <= n-3, any n-vertex graph that is not k-edge Hamiltonian contains at most max(g_t(n, k, 1), g_t(n, k, floor((n-1-k)/2))) t-stars, where g_t(n, k, i) = i * choose(i+k, t) + (n-2*i-k) * choose(n-i-1, t) + (i+k) * choose(n-1, t). This corresponds to the extremal graphs G(n, k, 1) and G(n, k, i_0).
proof_strategy: Induction on the number of vertices or edges, combined with structural graph theory techniques such as vertex deletion and edge shifting, reducing the problem to analyzing the specific extremal graphs G(n, k, 1) and G(n, k, i_0).
title: Conjecture on the Maximum Number of Stars in Non-k-Edge-Hamiltonian Graphs

catalog_references: De Bruijn and Erdős cake cutting
description: For any recipe σ of length p and r ≥ 1, if the number of periods m is at least 2⌈r/p⌉, then the asymptotic maximum-to-minimum ratio μ_r(σ) equals the greatest ratio that occurs during the phase with m periods.
proof_strategy: Formalize the sequence of cuts for a recipe σ, define the ratio μ_n_r of max to min sizes of r consecutive pieces, and show that the limsup μ_r equals the supremum of μ_n_r over the finite range of n corresponding to the phase with m periods.
title: Periodic Cake Cutting Phase Ratio

description: The minimal absolute value σ₅(n) of a non-vanishing sum of n fifth roots of unity is monotone non-increasing over congruence classes of n modulo 5. Furthermore, a strict decrease σ₅(n) > σ₅(n+5) occurs if and only if n+5 is of the form 5Fₘ, Lₘ, or 2Lₘ for some positive integer m, where Fₘ and Lₘ denote the m-th Fibonacci and Lucas numbers, respectively.
proof_strategy: Define the function σ₅(n) as the infimum of the absolute values of non-vanishing sums of n 5th roots of unity. Prove the monotonicity within congruence classes modulo 5 by constructing appropriate sums. Characterize the strict decreases by relating the problem to rational approximations of the golden ratio via continued fractions, using the specific properties of Fibonacci and Lucas numbers.
title: Monotonicity and Jumps of Minimal Absolute Values of Fifth Roots of Unity Sums

description: For every positive integer k, there exist infinitely many odd integers s such that the 5-rank of the Pólya group Po(K_s) of the Lecacheux quintic field K_s equals k. This strengthens the paper's result from '5-rank at least k for a set of positive density' to '5-rank exactly k for infinitely many parameters', providing a complete stratification of achievable 5-ranks in this family.
proof_strategy: Partition the parameter space of odd integers s by the exact 5-rank of Po(K_s). For each target rank k, use the parametric structure of Lecacheux fields to identify congruence conditions on s that control which prime ideals above 5 generate the characteristic ideals. Show that the conditions for achieving rank exactly k (rather than at least k) are satisfied for infinitely many s by applying Chebotarev's density theorem in the cyclotomic field Q(ζ₅) and its subfields. The key step is excluding 'excess rank' contributions by ensuring that only k of the possible 5-adic prime ideals contribute non-trivially to the Pólya group, which can be achieved by imposing suitable splitting conditions on s.
title: Exact 5-Rank Realization for Pólya Groups of Lecacheux Quintic Fields

description: For the morphisms $\phi$ (where $\phi(a)=abc, \phi(b)=ac, \phi(c)=b$) and $\mu$ (where $\mu(a)=a, \mu(b)=b, \mu(c)=cbbbc$), let $x'_k = \phi^k(a)$ and $x_k = \mu(x'_k)$. The conjecture states that for any $k \ge 0$, if a $3^+$-parameterized square $w = uv$ with $|u|=|v| \ge 3$ exists as a subword of $x_k$, then $u=v$, meaning there are no non-standard $3^+$-parameterized squares.
proof_strategy: Define the morphisms $\phi$ and $\mu$ on a ternary alphabet. Prove that any parameterized square of length $\ge 6$ in $x_k$ implies $u=v$ by analyzing the local structure around occurrences of 'c' and 'bb', leveraging the fact that $x'_k$ is square-free and the specific substitution properties of $\mu$.
title: Absence of Non-Standard 3+-Parameterized Squares in x_k

description: The regularized coupling of two vector-valued weight 3/2 mock Eisenstein series (which individually yield depth one mock modular forms) produces a depth two mock modular form of weight 3. Specifically, the completion of this coupled object satisfies a $\bar{\partial}$-equation whose shadow is a linear combination of tensor products of depth one mock Eisenstein series and holomorphic modular forms.
proof_strategy: Formalize the definition of depth two mock modular forms and the Eisenstein coupling operator. Compute the Fourier expansion of the coupled series and verify its $\bar{\partial}$-equation using the known analytic properties of mock Eisenstein series and Rankin-Selberg integrals.
title: Depth Two Mock Modularity of Coupled Mock Eisenstein Series

description: For integers $r \ge 2$ and $t_3, \dots, t_{r+1} \ge 2$, the maximum number of edges in a non-$r$-partite $K_{1,1,t_3,\dots,t_{r+1}}$-free graph of order $n$ is exactly $|E(T_{n,r})| - \lfloor n/r \rfloor + 2(t_{\min}-1)$ for all sufficiently large $n$, where $T_{n,r}$ is the Turán graph and $t_{\min} = \min\{t_3,\dots,t_{r+1}\}$.
proof_strategy: Define the non-$r$-partite Turán number, construct the extremal graph by modifying the Turán graph $T_{n,r}$, and prove the upper bound using spectral graph theory and the structural condition on the sub-decomposition family of $K_{1,1,t_3,\dots,t_{r+1}}$.
title: Exact Non-r-Partite Turán Number for Complete Multipartite Graphs

description: Within the class of distance-hereditary graphs, balanced graphs coincide exactly with hereditary clique-Helly graphs, and equivalently with graphs forbidding the complement of 3K₂ as an induced subgraph. This conjecture formalizes the main theorem of the paper: for every distance-hereditary graph G, G is balanced if and only if G contains no induced copy of 3K₂ (the complement of three disjoint edges, i.e., the graph on six vertices partitioned into three independent edges, complemented).
proof_strategy: Formalize the three key definitions (distance-hereditary, balanced via clique-matrix condition, hereditary clique-Helly) and the graph 3K₂-bar. Prove the equivalence in two directions: (1) If a distance-hereditary graph G is balanced, it contains no induced 3K₂-bar (using the known result that balanced implies no extended odd sun, and that 3K₂-bar is an extended odd sun within distance-hereditary graphs). (2) If a distance-hereditary graph G contains no induced 3K₂-bar, then it is hereditary clique-Helly and hence balanced. The key structural lemma is that within distance-hereditary graphs, the only minimal obstruction to balancedness that is also an extended odd sun is 3K₂-bar. Decompose the proof using the pruning-sequence characterization of distance-hereditary graphs to handle each attachment operation (twin, pendant) inductively.
title: Balanced equals hereditary clique-Helly within distance-hereditary graphs

description: In type A_n, the subalgebra B_aff of the affine Hecke algebra admits a canonical basis {b_{W_fin w}} indexed by cosets W_fin \ W_aff. The conjecture states that the structure constants of B_aff with respect to this canonical basis are polynomials in v with non-negative integer coefficients: for any two cosets W_fin w and W_fin w' in W_fin \ W_aff, the product b_{W_fin w} · b_{W_fin w'} = Σ c_{w,w'}^z · b_{W_fin z} where each c_{w,w'}^z ∈ Z_{≥0}[v]. This is the v-deformed analogue of the positivity of structure constants in the affine Fomin-Stanley subalgebra (equivalently, homology of the affine Grassmannian).
proof_strategy: First formalize the affine Weyl group W_aff = W_fin ⋉ Q∨ in type A_n as a Coxeter group with generators S_aff = S_fin ∪ {s_0}. Define the affine Hecke algebra H_aff over Z[v,v^{-1}] with Bernstein presentation and quadratic relations. Construct the pseudo-centralizer subalgebra B_aff as the subalgebra generated by appropriate elements arising from the DAHA centralizer construction. Prove the canonical basis exists (indexed by W_fin \ W_aff) by establishing a graded module structure and applying the bar-involution argument. Finally, establish positivity of structure constants using geometric arguments via the affine Grassmannian or combinatorial arguments via the v-deformed Pieri rule.
title: Positivity of structure constants for the canonical basis of the pseudo-centralizer subalgebra in type A

description: The oriented chromatic number of the directed Cartesian product C⃗₃ □ C⃗₄ of directed 3- and 4-cycles equals 7. That is, there exists a digraph homomorphism from C⃗₃ □ C⃗₄ to some 7-vertex tournament, but no digraph homomorphism from C⃗₃ □ C⃣₄ to any 6-vertex tournament. This finite combinatorial fact is the essential obstruction in the proof that the continuous oriented chromatic number of the directed Schreier graph F⃗(2^ℤ²) is 7: the torus tile C₃ □ C₄ is one of the Twelve Tiles, and ruling out 6-vertex tournaments as targets for this tile (along with the long tile) constitutes the core of the lower bound argument.
proof_strategy: Define the directed torus digraph C⃗₃ □ C⃗₄ on vertex set Z/3Z × Z/4Z with horizontal arcs (i,j)→(i+1,j) and vertical arcs (i,j)→(i,j+1). For the upper bound, explicitly construct a homomorphism to a 7-vertex tournament by assigning colors to each of the 12 vertices. For the lower bound, enumerate all 35 non-isomorphic strong tournaments on 6 vertices and verify that none admits a homomorphism from C⃗₃ □ C⃗₄. The 27 tournaments handled by order-energy and 4 by non-order energies yield to algebraic invariants formalizable as homomorphism obstructions; the remaining 4 require the diagonal marker propagation argument exploiting gcd(3,4)=1, which forces marker-set invariance under translation by 4 in Z/3Z—a contradiction for proper nonempty sets.
title: Oriented chromatic number of the directed torus C₃ □ C₄

description: For integers n > l ≥ 2, if E ⊆ ℝⁿ is a Borel set with Hausdorff dimension dim_H(E) > l+1, then for almost every V ∈ G(n,l), the orthogonal projection Π_V(E) has nonempty interior. This improves the Peres–Schlag exponent 2l to l+1, matching the sharp finite-field threshold established in the paper. The case l=1 is excluded since 2l = l+1 = 2 is already sharp by Besicovitch–Mattila constructions. For l ≥ 2, the gap between the known bound 2l and the conjectured bound l+1 remains open, and the paper's finite-field result strongly suggests l+1 is the true threshold.
proof_strategy: The finite-field proof shows the l+1 threshold arises from polynomial method arguments linked to Kakeya set bounds. To lift this to ℝⁿ: (1) discretize the Euclidean problem by replacing E with a δ-packing and passing to a finite-field model via rescaling and reduction mod p, (2) apply the finite-field sharp threshold result to obtain rich projections for the discretized set, (3) use Bourgain's framework reformulating Peres–Schlag in terms of L² bounds for maximal k-plane transforms controlled by Riesz energy, (4) combine with the best available Kakeya maximal L^p estimates (from BCCLXZ and related works) and the paper's maximal k-plane transform bounds to close the gap from 2l down to l+1. Guth's polynomial partitioning method may provide the continuous analogue of the polynomial method used in the finite-field setting.
title: Sharp Euclidean Peres–Schlag Threshold Equals l+1 for l ≥ 2

description: We conjecture that for each integer n≥3 the exponent 3/(2n‑1) in the finite‑field Peres‑Schlag theorem for product sets is optimal. More precisely, there exists a constant c_n > 0 such that for all sufficiently large primes p there is a subset A ⊂ ℤ_p with |A| ≤ c_n·p^{3/(2n‑1)} for which no choice of coefficients t_1,…,t_n ∈ ℤ_p yields a covering t_1A + … + t_nA = ℤ_p. Equivalently, the threshold cannot be lowered below 3/(2n‑1).
proof_strategy: To prove the conjecture one would construct, for each n, small subsets A ⊂ ℤ_p (for large p) that avoid being covered by any n‑term dilated sum. This would likely involve adapting known Kakeya‑type or cap‑set constructions to produce sets whose n‑fold linear images have small density. A successful construction would establish the sharpness of the exponent 3/(2n‑1). A disproof would require showing that any set of size ≈ p^{3/(2n‑1)} inevitably yields a covering, perhaps via Fourier‑analytic or algebraic‑geometric methods.
title: Sharpness of the finite‑field Peres‑Schlag exponent for product sets

description: Any finite group that can be expressed as the product of two dihedral subgroups is solvable. This extends the classical result of Kegel and Wielandt on the solvability of products of two nilpotent groups to the case of dihedral groups, noting that dihedral groups are solvable (specifically, metacyclic) but not necessarily nilpotent.
proof_strategy: Assume the group is non-solvable and consider a minimal counterexample, which must be an almost simple group. Then apply the classification of exact factorizations of almost simple groups (Li, Wang, Xia) and maximal factorizations (Liebeck, Praeger, Saxl) to show that no almost simple group can be factorized as a product of two dihedral subgroups, yielding a contradiction.
title: Solvability of Finite Bidihedral Groups

description: For any number field K and integer g ≥ 1, there exists a constant C depending only on K and g, such that the geometric étale fundamental group of the Néron model of any g-dimensional abelian variety over K has order at most C.
proof_strategy: Generalize the methods used for elliptic curves (which rely on Merel's torsion theorem) to higher dimensions, potentially by establishing a uniform lower bound on the Faltings height of abelian varieties over a fixed number field to apply Northcott finiteness uniformly across all isogenies.
title: Uniform Boundedness of Geometric Étale Fundamental Groups of Néron Models

description: For an r-periodic Riemann function f: ℤ² → ℤ with perfect matching weight W, the paper proves a Serre-type duality pairing H^i(ℳ_{W,0} ⊗ F) × Ext^{1-i}(F, ℳ_{W^∧_L, K}) → H^1(ω_W) ≅ k is perfect when L = K + 1 and F is a line bundle or skyscraper sheaf. The conjecture is that this pairing is perfect for ALL finite-type O_r-modules F (not just line bundles and skyscraper sheafs), making ω_W a genuine dualizing module in the sense of Serre duality on the five-point topological space.
proof_strategy: Classify all finite-type O_r-modules on the five-point space as extensions of line bundles and skyscraper sheaves, then use the long exact sequence in cohomology and Ext to reduce perfection of the pairing for arbitrary modules to the known cases via the five-lemma on the induced maps of pairings.
title: Serre Duality Perfection for All Coherent O_r-Modules on the Five-Point Space

description: Every admissible graph (a graph with no pendant path of length two, i.e., no path x-y-z with d(x)=1 and d(y)=2) admits a strong majority edge-coloring with at most 4 colors. A strong majority edge-coloring requires that for every edge e=uv and every color i, at most (d(u)+d(v))/2 - 1 edges adjacent to e receive color i. Kalinowski, Kamyczura, Pilśniak, and Woźniak originally proved 8 colors suffice and conjectured 4; the current paper improves the bound to 5, but the conjecture remains open.
proof_strategy: The case δ(G) ≥ 7 is already settled (4 colors suffice by KKPW). The remaining cases require handling admissible graphs with small minimum degree. A promising approach combines the Hilton–de Werra equitable edge-coloring tools with vertex-splitting arguments used in the 5-color proof, performing a more refined case analysis on the degree structure of low-degree vertices and their local neighborhoods. The key obstacle is ensuring no color dominates the neighborhood of any single edge when restricted to 4 colors.
title: Strong Majority Edge-Coloring Conjecture: Four Colors Suffice for Admissible Graphs

description: The line graph of the bipartite Kneser graph $BL_n(k-1,k)$ is an integral graph when $n = 2k-1$. That is, all eigenvalues of the adjacency matrix of the line graph of $BL_{2k-1}(k-1,k)$ are integers.
proof_strategy: Define the bipartite Kneser graph $BL_n(k-1,k)$ and its line graph. Show that for $n=2k-1$, the eigenvalues of $BL_n(k-1,k)$ are integers (specifically $\pm(k-j)$). Then, use the spectral properties of regular bipartite graphs and their line graphs to deduce that the eigenvalues of the line graph are integers.
title: Integrality of the Line Graph of Bipartite Kneser Graphs

description: For the unramified GU(1,n-1) Rapoport-Zink space at any parahoric level, every irreducible component of the Zariski closure of any basic EKOR stratum is smooth. The paper proves this for 'certain' EKOR strata; this conjecture asserts it holds for all basic EKOR strata. Since each basic EKOR stratum is a disjoint union of copies of a fine Deligne-Lusztig variety X_w(b), the conjecture reduces to showing that for every w in the relevant finite subset of the Iwahori-Weyl group, the irreducible components of the Zariski closure of X_w(b) in the Rapoport-Zink space are smooth. This would imply that all singularities of the basic locus arise purely from the crossing of EKOR stratum closures, with no intrinsic singularities on individual closure components.
proof_strategy: Decompose the closure of a basic EKOR stratum indexed by w into irreducible components using the identification with fine Deligne-Lusztig varieties. For each w, analyze the closure relations in the EKOR stratification poset and show that the boundary of X_w(b) in the Rapoport-Zink space is a union of smooth Deligne-Lusztig varieties of lower dimension. Use the group-theoretic description of the EKOR stratification via the Iwahori-Weyl group to reduce smoothness to a combinatorial condition on the Bruhat order. Verify this condition for all elements in the basic locus using the explicit description of admissible elements for GU(1,n-1).
title: Smoothness of irreducible components of basic EKOR stratum closures for GU(1,n-1)

description: Given a field E and a subgroup H of its automorphism group, for any element α in E with a finite H-orbit, the minimal polynomial of α over the fixed field E^H is exactly the orbit polynomial, defined as the product of linear factors (X - σ(α)) over the distinct elements of the H-orbit of α.
proof_strategy: 1. Define the orbit polynomial as the monic polynomial whose roots are exactly the elements of the H-orbit of α. 2. Prove its coefficients are invariant under the action of H, establishing that it is a polynomial over the fixed field E^H. 3. Prove it is irreducible over E^H by showing that any monic factor over E^H containing one root must contain all roots due to the transitive action of H on the orbit. 4. Conclude that this irreducible monic polynomial over E^H must be the minimal polynomial.
title: Orbit Polynomial as Minimal Polynomial

description: For every graph G, its line graph L(G) is chromatic-choosable: the list chromatic number of L(G) equals the chromatic number of L(G). Equivalently, for every graph G, the list chromatic index ch'(G) equals the chromatic index χ'(G). This is the List Coloring Conjecture, the central open problem in list-coloring. Galvin (1995) proved the bipartite case using the kernel method, showing ch'(G) = Δ(G) for bipartite multigraphs, but the general case remains wide open.
proof_strategy: First formalize the bipartite case (Galvin's theorem) as a stepping stone: orient edges of L(G) and show every induced subdigraph has a kernel, which forces choosability equal to max out-degree. This requires König's theorem for bipartite matching (already in Mathlib). The general case likely requires extending the kernel method or developing entirely new algebraic/topological techniques.
title: Line Graphs Are Chromatic-Choosable (List Coloring Conjecture)

description: For integers $g > k \ge 2$, the prime divisors of the minimal positive multiple $m_k(g)$ of the minimal class $\theta_k$ that is algebraic on a very general principally polarized abelian variety of dimension $g$ are exactly the primes $p \leq (k+1)/2$. This establishes the sharpness of the paper's lower bound, conjecturing that no prime $p > (k+1)/2$ divides $m_k(g)$.
proof_strategy: Extend the combinatorial analysis of $\mathbb{F}_p$-solutions of graphic matroids and their Albanese graphs to prove that no prime $p > (k+1)/2$ can divide $m_k(g)$, thereby establishing the exact equivalence for prime divisibility and confirming the lower bound is sharp.
title: Sharp Primorial Divisibility of Minimal Classes on Abelian Varieties

description: The authors propose Andrews-Gordon type series for level 2 standard modules of type $A^{(2)}_{2\ell-1}$ and prove the corresponding sum-product identities except for the family $A^{(2)}_{6n+3}$ (where $\ell = 3n+2$). The conjecture is that for $A^{(2)}_{6n+3}$, the proposed Andrews-Gordon type infinite series equals the product side given by the principal character $\frac{Q(q^{6n+6}, q^b)}{(q^2; q^2)_\infty}$, where $Q(w,x)$ is the quintuple product.
proof_strategy: Extend the Bailey lattice techniques or vertex operator algebra constructions used for the other cases in the paper to overcome the specific algebraic obstructions for the $A^{(2)}_{6n+3}$ family, potentially by identifying new Bailey pairs relative to the moduli that cause the current method to fail.
title: Sum-Product Identity for Level 2 Standard Modules of Type $A^{(2)}_{6n+3}$

description: Conjecture: For every P₄‑tidy graph G and any two independent sets I, I' of G with |I| = |I'|, there exists a token‑sliding sequence transforming I into I'. This would extend the polynomial‑time algorithm for the reconfiguration problem on P₄‑tidy graphs to a structural connectivity result for equal‑sized independent sets.
proof_strategy: Use the substitution decomposition (modular decomposition) of P₄‑tidy graphs. Prove the conjecture by induction on the decomposition tree: show that the property holds for prime, parallel, and series nodes, and that token‑sliding moves can be lifted/composed across the decomposition. For prime nodes, exploit the bounded number of P₄’s and the known structure of P₄‑tidy primes to construct explicit sliding sequences.
title: Reachability of equal-size independent sets in P₄‑tidy graphs under token sliding

description: A real quadratic field K = Q(√D) satisfies Hammarhjelm's condition if its ring of integers has unique factorization and the Minkowski lattice f(O_K) contains no point in the open rectangle (1, λ) × (-1, 1), where λ > 1 is the fundamental unit. The theorem states that exactly seven such fields exist, corresponding to squarefree D ∈ {2, 5, 13, 29, 53, 173, 293}.
proof_strategy: First build infrastructure for Minkowski embeddings of rings of integers of real quadratic fields, fundamental units, and the class number formula. Verify the seven cases individually (computable). For the finiteness/classification, formalize the regulator bound implied by Condition H, apply the class number formula to force large class numbers, and reduce to Biro's classification of class number one fields in Yokoi's family for the critical case.
title: Classification of real quadratic fields satisfying Hammarhjelm's condition

description: For every positive integer n, the partition λ_n consisting of ⌊n/2⌋ parts of size 2 and, if n is odd, one additional part of size 1, belongs to the set Ω_2(n) of irreducible constituents of the 2-Sylow permutation character of the symmetric group S_n. This would show that the upper bound ⌈n/2⌉ on the number of parts of partitions in Ω_2(n) (Proposition big) is sharp and is attained by this explicit partition.
proof_strategy: Use the explicit description of the 2-Sylow subgroup of S_n as an iterated wreath product and the Murnaghan-Nakayama rule to compute the multiplicity of the irreducible character χ^{λ_n} in the permutation character (1_P)↑^{S_n}. Alternatively, use the characterization of Ω_2(n) via 2-quotients of partitions (as in [G17]) and verify that the 2-quotient of λ_n satisfies the required condition. Another approach is to use the known results on the restriction of irreducible characters to Sylow 2-subgroups and the fact that λ_n is a partition with all parts ≤ 2.
title: The all-twos partition achieves the maximum number of parts in Ω₂(n)

description: There exists a graph G without a cycle of length d such that at least cd n edge deletions are required to transform G into a graph where each connected component has a vertex cover of size at most (1+c)d.
proof_strategy: Construct a specific graph achieving the lower bound via Pokrovskiy's structure theorem
title: Tightness of Edge Deletion Bound in Hyperstability Extension of Erdős-Gallai Theorem

description: Conjecture that for any fixed genus g > 0, there exists a constant C_g > 0 such that the spectral gap γ_{n,g} of the fixed genus chord swap chain on chord diagrams with n chords and genus g satisfies γ_{n,g} ≥ C_g / n for all n > 2g.
proof_strategy: Establish a conductance lower bound via a suitable coupling argument that relates chord swaps to graph-theoretic moves, and then use known inequalities to translate this into a polynomial lower bound on the spectral gap for fixed genus.
title: Polynomial spectral gap lower bound for fixed genus chord swap chain

proof_strategy: induction
title: Finitely Generated Schottky Group

description: Conjecture: The properly normalized extremal fluctuations of black hole microstate counts in quantum gravity converge in distribution to the Gumbel extreme value distribution. Specifically, let N(Λ) denote the count of microstates with energy below Λ for a holographic CFT with large central charge c. Define the extremal fluctuation ΔN_c = max_Λ(N(Λ) - E[N(Λ)])/√(Var[N(Λ)]) over Λ in an interval. Then as c→∞, exp(-e^(-x)) = lim_{c→∞} P(ΔN_c ≤ x) in distribution. This predicts a universal tail exponent α=1 for the log-correlated field universality class.
domain_bridges: Quantum Field Theory (operator counting in CFT)
proof_strategy: Establish the connection via holography: (1) Prove interval counting for high-dimension CFT primaries follows log-correlated field statistics, (2) Show the extremal process converges to Gumbel by analyzing the correlation structure of the underlying Gaussian free field, (3) Translate to AdS side via HKLL reconstruction to bound semiclassical path integral resolution. Use modular invariance and sparseness conditions to control the tail behavior rigorously.
title: Gumbel Distribution for Black Hole Microstate Extremal Fluctuations

description: For any matroid of rank r ≤ k, any two pairs of bases with the same multiset union can be transformed into each other via a sequence of symmetric exchanges.
proof_strategy: Inductive argument on rank bounds combined with matroid minors analysis
title: Symmetric Exchange Generation in Rank-Bounded Matroids

description: The spectral inequality equivalence for Sidorenko-type inequalities in admissible classes fails for certain bipartite graphs outside the range v(H) ≤ e(H). Specifically, for the 5-vertex path graph H (a tree with 5 vertices and 4 edges), there exists an admissible class C (e.g., the class of doubly nonnegative graphons) such that the spectral inequality holds for all W ∈ C, but H is not C-Sidorenko.
domain_bridges: Spectral radius vs. edge density relationships
proof_strategy: Construct a doubly nonnegative graphon W where the spectral inequality t(H,W) ≥ ρ(W)^{2e(H)-v(H)} p(W)^{v(H)-e(H)} holds but t(H,W) < p(W)^{e(H)} fails, demonstrating the equivalence's optimality in the v(H) ≤ e(H) range.
title: Spectral Transfer Sharpness for Trees Beyond the Sidorenko Range

description: We conjecture that for any monic polynomial P (not necessarily coprime to A^2‑1) the μ‑ and λ‑invariants of the Iwasawa module generated by the spectral resultant R_{X,P} are given by a precise Kida‑type formula involving the p‑adic valuations of R_{X,P} at all torsion characters, with an explicit correction term accounting for the Bass factor A^2‑1. This extends the leading asymptotic growth law proved in the coprime case.
proof_strategy: The proof would proceed by (1) constructing the Iwasawa module M as the Fitting module of the spectral resultant using the universal Grover‑Ihara polynomial; (2) applying the structure theorem for finitely generated Δ_₂[[Γ]]‑modules to express μ(M) and λ(M) in terms of elementary divisors; (3) evaluating the resultant at torsion characters χ∈̀_hat{Δ}_₂^× and showing via equivariant descent that the elementary divisors are precisely the values v_p(R(χ)); (4) incorporating the Bass factor (A^2‑1) by factoring det P(U_n) into a coprime part and a power of the Bass factor, and comparing the resulting contributions to the λ‑term. The key technical step is to prove an equivariant Kida formula for the spectral resultant without integrality assumptions, using the factorization for p‑group covers from the paper and a careful analysis of the local units at χ(1)=±1.
title: Extended μ-λ Formula for Spectral Resultants of Grover Walks on Graph Towers

description: Constructs two nine-line arrangements in \(\mathbb{P}^2\) with isomorphic intersection lattices but distinct minimal degrees of Jacobian relations (mdr). The configurations differ in their homological types, where one is plus-one generated and the other has type 2B, validating distinct Jacobian syzygy structures. The example refutes the conjecture that mdr is combinatorially determined when mdr < d/2.

proof_strategy: Explicit construction of arrangements with controlled intersection multiplicities, followed by computation of \(\mdr(f)\) via graded module generation and analysis of Jacobian syzygies using symbolic computation in Lean 4.

description: For positive integers m and nonnegative integers n, k, let r_m(n,k) be the number of ordered partitions of an n-element set with exactly k blocks of size at least m. The bivariate exponential generating function F_m(x,y) = ∑_{n,k≥0} r_m(n,k) x^n/n! y^k is given by F_m(x,y) = 1 / (1 - A_m(x) - y B_m(x)), where A_m(x) = ∑_{i=1}^{m-1} x^i/i! and B_m(x) = e^x - 1 - A_m(x).
domain_bridges: Stirling numbers of the second kind
proof_strategy: Interpret r_m(n,k) as counting labelled structures: an ordered partition where each block is either a 'non-tie' of size < m (weight 1) or a 'tie' of size ≥ m (weight y). The exponential generating function for non-tie blocks is A_m(x), for tie blocks is B_m(x). A sequence of such blocks has EGF 1/(1 - (A_m(x) + y B_m(x))). Equating coefficients yields the formula.
title: Bivariate Exponential Generating Function for Snail Race Outcomes

description: For a real quadratic field K of narrow class number one and a fundamental discriminant D, the generalized Hurwitz class number H_g(D) associated with K is equal to half the class number of a specific quartic CM field F_D constructed from D and K.
proof_strategy: Verify the conjectured formula by computing class numbers of explicitly constructed quartic CM fields and comparing them to the generalized Hurwitz class numbers defined via the trace formula. This requires formalizing quartic field construction, class group computations, and the definition of H_g(D) in Lean.
title: Generalized Hurwitz Class Number Formula for Quartic CM Fields

description: The integral ∫₁ˣ D(t)/t² dt remains negative for all x ≥ 1, where D(x) = Σ_{n≤x} σ(n) - x²ζ(2)/2 represents the error in the average order of the sum-of-divisors function. While the paper proves this for x ≥ 650, we conjecture that the negativity holds universally for all x ≥ 1, indicating a persistent systematic bias in the error term that complements the known asymptotic behavior.
proof_strategy: Verify the conjecture computationally for x ∈ [1, 650) by establishing explicit bounds on D(t) in this range, then combine with the asymptotic result from the paper. The key insight is that the weight (1-x/n) in the smoothed sum eliminates the difficult ψ-term, making the error term fundamentally more tractable than in the classical Walfisz problem.
title: Sign of the Smoothed Sum-of-Divisors Error Integral

description: For the elliptic curve E_7: y^2 = x^3 + 49/4 over the rational numbers, let P_7 = (84, 756) be the rational point corresponding to the cube sum 2^3 + (-1)^3 = 7. The explicit Gross-Zagier formula from Yin's paper implies that L'(E_7, 1) / Omega_7 = (1/2) * hat_h_Q(P_7), where Omega_7 is the real Neron period of E_7 and hat_h_Q is the Neron-Tate height over Q.
proof_strategy: Compute the Hasse-Weil L-function derivative at s=1 and the Neron-Tate height of the explicitly defined rational point P_7 = (84, 756) on E_7, and verify their equality using the explicit formula and height computations outlined in Yin's paper.
title: Explicit Gross-Zagier Formula for p=7

description: The shifted $t$-Schur function $\mathcal{Q}_\lambda(X;t)$, generated by the modified odd Greaves--Jing--Zhu operator $\mathcal{Y}_t(z) = \mathcal{R}_t \Phi(z) \mathcal{R}_t^{-1}$ (where $\mathcal{R}_t$ rescales each odd power sum $p_n \mapsto (1-t^n)p_n$ and $\Phi(z)$ is the classical Schur $Q$ vertex operator), equals the classical Schur $Q$-function $Q_\lambda$ under the plethystic substitution $X \mapsto X - tX$. Equivalently, $\mathcal{R}_t Q_\lambda(X) = Q_\lambda[X - tX]$ for every strict partition $\lambda$ and formal parameter $t$. This encapsulates the conjugation relation and the resulting plethystic interpretation of the modified operator's spectrum.
proof_strategy: First formalize the odd power-sum ring $\Gamma_t = \mathbb{Q}(t)[p_1, p_3, p_5, \ldots]$ as a graded Hopf algebra over $\mathbb{Q}(t)$. Define the diagonal automorphism $\mathcal{R}_t$ rescaling $p_n \mapsto (1-t^n)p_n$ for odd $n$, and prove it is a Hopf algebra automorphism. Define the classical Schur $Q$ vertex operator $\Phi(z)$ via its exponential form in creation/annihilation operators on $\Gamma_t$. Construct the modified operator $\mathcal{Y}_t(z)$ and prove the conjugation identity $\mathcal{Y}_t(z) = \mathcal{R}_t \Phi(z) \mathcal{R}_t^{-1}$ by verifying that $\mathcal{R}_t p_n \mathcal{R}_t^{-1} = (1-t^n)p_n$ and $\mathcal{R}_t (\partial/p_n) \mathcal{R}_t^{-1} = (1-t^n)^{-1} \partial/p_n$. The plethystic identity then follows by applying both sides to the vacuum vector and extracting coefficients indexed by strict partitions, using that $\mathcal{R}_t^{-1}|0\rangle = |0\rangle$.
title: Shifted t-Schur plethystic identity via modified odd operator conjugation

description: The paper proves, assuming the Generalized Riemann Hypothesis (GRH), that if K is a totally real Galois number field of degree n ≥ 3 and p is an odd rational prime which does not split completely in K, then every generating set of the ray class group Cl_K^{(p)^N} with modulus (p)^N is a Euclidean system. This conjecture posits that the GRH assumption can be removed, asserting that the statement holds unconditionally.
proof_strategy: The existing proof relies on GRH via Artin's generalized primitive root conjecture to guarantee the existence of primes with specific norm properties that enable the Euclidean division. An unconditional proof would likely require circumventing GRH by developing new analytic number theory techniques to establish stronger lower bounds on the relevant prime counting functions, or by discovering an alternative algebraic mechanism for constructing the Euclidean norm function for ray classes.
title: Unconditional Euclidean Systems for Ray Classes in Totally Real Galois Fields

description: For every n ≥ 0, the n-th row generating function of the square of the Eulerian triangle—defined as the polynomial ∑_k (∑_j A(n,j)·A(j,k)) x^k where A(n,k) is the Eulerian number counting permutations of [n] with k descents—has only real roots. This extends the paper's results on powers of Pascal, Stirling, and Narayana triangles to the still-open Eulerian case.
proof_strategy: Attempt to decompose the Eulerian triangle square as a product of triangles whose individual real-rootedness preservation is known, or extend the rectangular additive convolution framework to construct an interlacing chain for the squared Eulerian row generating functions. Alternatively, establish that the Eulerian triangle square arises from a Narayana-type transformation applied to a suitable real-rooted polynomial.
title: Real-rootedness of the square of the Eulerian triangle

description: For all integers a, b with 3 ≤ a ≤ b, there exists a constant C > 0 such that for any n-vertex graph G that is K_{3,b+1}-free, the number of labeled copies of K_{a,b} in G is at most C * n^3. This captures the main asymptotic upper bound result of the paper, resolving the generalized Turán problem for these parameters.
proof_strategy: Formalize the definitions of K_{s,t}-free graphs and the counting of labeled subgraphs isomorphic to K_{a,b}. Apply the Kővári–Sós–Turán theorem and double counting arguments, bounding the number of K_{a,b} copies by considering the number of common neighbors of a-sets of vertices.
title: Upper Bound on Generalized Turán Number ex(n, K_{a,b}, K_{3,b+1})

description: The sequence of total d-Hoggatt numbers, defined as the row sums H_d(n) = sum_{k=0}^n H_d(n,k), is infinitely log-concave for all d >= 1. The paper proves the infinite log-concavity of the row and column sequences of the d-Hoggatt triangle. However, the infinite log-concavity of the total d-Hoggatt numbers remains open, encompassing the unresolved infinite log-concavity of the Baxter numbers for d=3 and Catalan numbers for d=2.
proof_strategy: Leverage the real-rootedness of the row generating functions (proven by Dilks and Fang-Zhang-Zhao) combined with the theory of multiplier sequences or Pólya frequency sequences to establish the infinite log-concavity of the total sums. Alternatively, employ recurrence relations and induction with tight asymptotic bounds derived from the asymptotic normality of the row sequences.
title: Infinite Log-Concavity of Total d-Hoggatt Numbers

description: For an algebraically closed field F of characteristic 0, integer k ≥ 18, and nonzero polynomial n ∈ F[X], any finite set A ⊂ F[X] with property D_k(n) (meaning ab+n is a k-th power for all distinct a,b ∈ A) satisfies |A| ≤ 6, unless n is a k-th power and A consists of scalar multiples of a square root of n.
proof_strategy: Formalize the determinant criterion for Diophantine tuples and generalizations of the Mason-Stothers theorem over polynomial rings. Combine these with the Combinatorial Nullstellensatz to derive a contradiction if |A| > 6 outside the exceptional family.
title: Absolute Bound for Generalized Polynomial Diophantine Tuples

description: For any fixed 0 < q < 1, as the prime modulus r → ∞ and x → ∞ with x ≤ r^{1/2-ε} for fixed ε > 0, the normalized 2q-th moment (1/(r-1))∑_{χ mod r} |∑_{n≤x} χ(n)|^{2q} / x^q converges to an explicit constant C_q equal to the corresponding moment for partial sums of a Steinhaus random multiplicative function. This extends the paper's order-of-magnitude result (which shows the moment is Θ(x^q)) to a precise asymptotic, confirming the heuristic that short character sums behave like random multiplicative functions in the low-moment regime.
proof_strategy: Extend the barrier-adjusted Perron integral comparison method from the current paper to obtain precise asymptotics rather than order-of-magnitude bounds. Key steps: (1) show the barrier adjustment in I(χ) contributes at most o(1) to the normalized moment, allowing direct comparison with the unadjusted integral; (2) establish concentration of the character sum moment around its mean using the fourth moment bounds already developed in the paper; (3) identify the limiting constant via the random multiplicative function model by proving the Euler product structure of the moments converges to the random model value, leveraging the fact that for 0<q<1 the moments are dominated by typical rather than extreme behavior.
title: Asymptotic equivalence of low moments of character sums and random multiplicative sums

description: Let $M$ be a piecewise-linear manifold of dimension $d \ge 1$. If $S$ and $T$ are two locally finite triangulations of $M$, then $S$ and $T$ are related by a locally finite sequence of bistellar moves (Pachner moves).
proof_strategy: Utilize the paper's result that two triangulations with a common subdivision have a common $\omega$-stellar subdivision. Then, show that the $\omega$-stellar subdivision can be reached from the original triangulations via locally finite sequences of bistellar moves, extending Pachner's theorem to infinite complexes by controlling the locality of the inverse stellar moves.
title: Infinite Pachner's Theorem for Locally Finite Triangulations

description: The maximum cardinality F(N) of a Sidon subset of {0, 1, ..., N-1} satisfies F(N) ≤ N^(1/2) + 0.94601 N^(1/4) + O(1). This conjecture proposes formalizing this main theorem, which improves the previously best-known coefficient of the N^(1/4) term from 0.97633 to 0.94601. The proof relies on a vector-valued smoothing lemma and a finite rational certificate verified by exact arithmetic, both of which are highly amenable to formalization in Lean 4.
proof_strategy: 1. Define Sidon sets and the function F(N). 2. Formalize the multi-kernel smoothing lemma (Lemma 1) which convexifies the boundary covering problem by placing smoothed indicator functions in a weighted Hilbert direct sum. 3. Extract and formalize the specific rational parameters of the finite certificate provided in the paper. 4. Verify the exact arithmetic constraints of the certificate within Lean 4. 5. Combine the smoothing lemma and the verified certificate to establish the asymptotic inequality with the explicit constant 0.94601.
title: Explicit Secondary Term Bound for Sidon Sets

description: For every prime p and every pro-p Demushkin group G with invariant q(G), the differential graded algebra C(G, 𝔽_p) of continuous cochains is A₃-formal if and only if q(G) ≠ 3. The 'if' direction is established by the present paper (for p = 2) combined with prior work (for odd p), while the 'only if' direction—that the pro-3 Demushkin group with q = 3 fails to be A₃-formal—remains open and would complete the classification.
proof_strategy: The 'if' direction follows from computing the Benson–Krause–Schwede canonical class for Demushkin groups with q ≠ 3, interpreting it as defining systems of higher Massey products (the key innovation for p = 2). The 'only if' direction for q = 3 requires showing the canonical class is nonzero for the pro-3 Demushkin group with q = 3, likely via an explicit cocycle-level computation of the universal triple Massey product or by constructing a non-trivial defining system that obstructs A₃-formality.
title: Complete characterization of A₃-formality for Demushkin groups

description: For all positive integers $n$ and $r$, and all partitions $\mu, \lambda \vdash n$, the polynomial $(-1)^{|\mu|-\ell(\mu)}\langle \nabla^r m_\mu, s_\lambda \rangle$ has nonnegative integer coefficients, i.e., belongs to $\mathbb{N}[q,t]$. This generalizes the 1999 conjecture of Bergeron, Garsia, Haiman, and Tesler (which corresponds to the case $r=1$), recently proven in the paper.
proof_strategy: Formalize the ring of symmetric functions, the Hall inner product, and the modified Macdonald basis. Define the nabla operator and the Haglund-Morse-Zabrocki operators $C_\alpha$. Establish the expansion of $(-1)^{|\mu|-\ell(\mu)}m_\mu$ in the $C_\alpha(1)$ basis with nonnegative coefficients in $\mathbb{Q}_{\ge 0}[q]$. Finally, combine this expansion with the compositional shuffle theorem and the Schur positivity of LLT polynomials to conclude the nonnegativity of the inner product.
title: Generalized BGHT Signed Schur Positivity Conjecture

description: For any finite set F = {f₁, ..., fₙ} ⊆ ℝᴹ and map Φ: ℝᴹ → ℝᴹ', the number of Φ-separable dichotomies C_F satisfies C(κ, n) ≤ C_F ≤ C(ρ, n), where ρ is the rank and κ is the Kruskal rank of {Φ(fₖ)}ₖ₌₁ⁿ, and C(d, n) = 2·∑_{k=0}^{min(d,n)-1} binom(n-1, k) is Cover's counting function. This generalizes Cover's 1965 result by replacing the general position assumption with structural degeneracy measures.
proof_strategy: Adapt Cover's inductive argument on point insertion: establish base cases for degenerate configurations, then show that inserting a point whose image under Φ lies in a subspace spanned by k previous images can increase dichotomy count by at most a factor governed by rank ρ, and at least by a factor governed by Kruskal rank κ. The key lemma is that the number of new dichotomies created by inserting a point equals twice the number of existing dichotomies that have the new point on their boundary, which is bounded by C(κ, n-1) from below and C(ρ, n-1) from above.
title: Kruskal-Rank and Rank Bounds on Separable Dichotomy Counts
