description: The Extended 1-2-3 Conjecture posits that for any finite nonempty set $A \subseteq \mathbb{N}$ and any positive integer $n$, the symmetric difference $A \Delta 2A \Delta \cdots \Delta nA$ contains at least $n$ elements. While recently proven for all $n$ sufficiently large (specifically $n \ge 2(3^{80}-321)$) and for $n \le 6$, the conjecture remains open in general, particularly for intermediate values of $n$.
proof_strategy: Formalize the known small cases ($n \le 6$) and the asymptotic result, then bridge the remaining gap $7 \le n < 2(3^{80}-321)$ by either refining the analytic bounds on rough numbers to lower the constant $N$, or developing new combinatorial arguments for intermediate values of $n$.
title: Extended 1-2-3 Conjecture for Symmetric Differences

description: For p an odd prime, k ≥ 2 an even integer, and a_p in the algebraic closure of Q_p with v(a_p) > 0 and v(a_p) not an integer (i.e., the slope is fractional), the mod p semisimplified reduction V̄_{k,a_p} of the two-dimensional crystalline representation V_{k,a_p} of G_{Q_p} is irreducible. This folklore conjecture is partially established in the paper for fractional slopes less than p-2 and sufficiently large even weights k under a slope assumption on bad congruence classes of k mod p.
proof_strategy: First formalize filtered phi-modules and the equivalence between crystalline representations and admissible filtered phi-modules (Fontaine's theory). Then build the mod p local Langlands correspondence for GL_2(Q_p) in Lean, establishing the correspondence between Galois representations and representations of GL_2(F_p). The irreducibility for even weight and fractional slope follows by analyzing which mod p representations of GL_2(Q_p) can arise via the correspondence, showing that reducible reductions correspond to integer slopes when k is even.
title: Irreducibility of mod p reductions of crystalline representations at fractional slope and even weight

description: For any fixed $k \ge 4$, there exists a natural number $N$ such that for all $n \ge N$ and integers $q$, if $q > \sqrt[k-1]{(k-1)\left(\frac{2(k-1)}{k}\right)^{k-2}n^{k-2}}$, then Breaker has a constructive winning strategy in the Maker-Breaker $C_k$-game on the complete graph $K_n$ with bias $q$.
proof_strategy: Define the Maker-Breaker game state as a pair of disjoint edge subsets of $K_n$. Formalize the specific potential function $\Phi$ for $C_k$ introduced by Glazik and Srivastav. Prove that Breaker's constructive strategy of selecting edges to minimize the potential guarantees that the potential remains bounded, which strictly implies that Maker cannot claim all edges of any copy of $C_k$.
title: Constructive Breaker Winning Strategies in the Maker-Breaker $C_k$-Game

description: The ranges of the lower and upper Wythoff-Fibonacci sequences, A* and B*, form a partition of the set of natural numbers. This means every natural number n >= 1 belongs to exactly one of the two sets.
proof_strategy: Formalize the Beatty sequences a(n) and b(n) using the golden ratio floor functions, define the epsilon correction using Fibonacci numbers, and establish the partition property by proving disjointness and covering, leveraging the lemma relating a(F_k), b(F_{k-1}), and b(F_k), a(F_{k+1}).
title: Wythoff-Fibonacci Partition of Natural Numbers

description: For the uniformly oriented A_n quiver, the number R_n of extension-closed additive subcategories of its representation category satisfies R_n ≥ F_{2n+2} for all n ≥ 0, where F_k is the k-th Fibonacci number (F_0 = 0, F_1 = 1). This conjecture strengthens the informal connection between OEIS A393920 and the Fibonacci sequence A000045 established in the paper, asserting a concrete exponential lower bound that reflects the shared growth structure. The recurrence in Proposition 3.2 and the combinatorial decomposition of R(n)_k suggest an inductive proof strategy comparing the recurrence for R_n against the Fibonacci doubling identity.
proof_strategy: Proceed by strong induction on n. The base cases n = 0, 1, 2 are verified by direct computation using the known initial values of R_n and F_{2n+2}. For the inductive step, use the recurrence R_n = Σ_{k=0}^{n+1} r(n,k) from the paper together with the recurrence for r(n,k) in Proposition 3.2. Lower-bound each r(n,k) term using the inductive hypothesis applied to the sub-quantities r(n-j-2,i) and p(j,k), then compare against the Fibonacci doubling identity F_{2n+2} = F_{2n+1} + F_{2n} = 3F_{2n-2} + 2F_{2n-3} to close the induction.
title: Fibonacci Lower Bound for Extension-Closed Subcategories of Type A_n

description: For the longest element w_0 in the Coxeter group B_n and any Coxeter element c, the normalized volume of the type B c-Birkhoff polytope equals the number of linear extensions of the heap poset Heap(c, w_0). This follows from the unimodular equivalence established in the paper and the classical result that the normalized volume of an order polytope equals the number of linear extensions of the underlying poset, but making the equality explicit and computable provides a concrete formalization target.
proof_strategy: First formalize heap posets Heap(c, w) for Coxeter group B_n, then define the type B c-Birkhoff polytope as the convex hull of appropriate permutation matrices corresponding to elements below w_0 in Bruhat order. Construct the explicit unimodular transformation to the order polytope of Heap(c, w_0). The normalized volume equality then follows from unimodular invariance of Ehrhart polynomials and the Stanley's result that the normalized volume of an order polytope is the number of its linear extensions.
title: Normalized volume of type B c-Birkhoff polytopes equals linear extension count of heap posets

description: The paper proves that the average absolute character sum over y-smooth numbers is o(√Ψ(x,y)) when q ≥ x^{1+ε}. This conjecture asserts that the same sub-square-root bound holds at the critical threshold q ≥ x (i.e., ε = 0), with a concrete saving factor. Specifically: for every ε > 0, there exists x₀(ε) such that for all x ≥ x₀, all primes q ≥ x, and all y with (log x)⁶ ≤ y ≤ x^{1/(32 log log x)}, the average absolute smooth character sum satisfies (1/(q-1)) Σ_{χ mod q, χ≠χ₀} |Σ_{n≤x, P(n)≤y} χ(n)| ≤ (1−ε)√Ψ(x,y). This extends the paper's main theorem from q ≥ x^{1+ε} to the boundary case q ≥ x, which is the natural threshold where the problem transitions from trivial to nontrivial.
proof_strategy: Adapt the paper's connection between character sums and Steinhaus random multiplicative functions. The key step is establishing the moment identity (1/φ(q))Σ_χ|Σ_{n≤x,P(n)≤y}χ(n)|^{2k} = E|Σ_{n≤x,P(n)≤y,(n,q)=1}f(n)|^{2k} for q ≥ x, which requires careful treatment of the coprimality condition at the boundary. Then leverage the authors' prior result on random multiplicative functions over smooths to extract the sub-square-root saving, combined with Harper's hypercontractivity machinery to control higher moments at the critical regime.
title: Sub-square-root bound for smooth character sums at the critical threshold

description: Any deterministic finite automaton (DFA) that correctly solves the Kochen-Specker problem (KSP) for a simple exclusivity graph G must possess at least χ(G) internal states. The KSP is defined as a language recognition task over the vertices of G, where strings of identical vertices are accepted, and strings of adjacent vertices are rejected.
proof_strategy: Proceed by contradiction. Assume the DFA has fewer than χ(G) states. The initial transition function maps each vertex v to an internal state δ(s_0, v). Because the number of states is less than the chromatic number, this mapping cannot form a valid vertex coloring. By the pigeonhole principle, there must exist an edge (v_A, v_B) in G such that both vertices map to the same internal state s_col. Show that the state reached after reading v_A from s_col must be in the accept set (from the string v_A v_A) but also not in the accept set (from the string v_B v_A), yielding a contradiction.
title: DFA State Complexity Lower Bound for the Kochen-Specker Problem

description: Every brick distinct from K_4, C_6_bar, and the Petersen graph, in which every b-invariant edge is a forcing edge, is near-bipartite. This conjecture, if true, would reduce the full Lucchesi–Murty characterization problem to the near-bipartite case already solved in this paper, by showing that no non-near-bipartite brick (beyond the three exceptions) can have the property that all its b-invariant edges are forcing edges.
proof_strategy: Assume for contradiction that there exists a non-near-bipartite brick G (distinct from the three exceptions) where every b-invariant edge is forcing. Use the fact that non-near-bipartite bricks contain two vertex-disjoint odd cycles whose vertex deletion leaves a graph with a perfect matching (negation of solidity). Apply the tight cut decomposition to identify structural constraints on b-invariant edges in such bricks, and leverage counting arguments on perfect matchings through these odd cycles to construct a b-invariant edge that must lie in at least two perfect matchings, contradicting the forcing property.
title: Near-bipartite reduction for the Lucchesi–Murty property

description: For the Boolean lattice B_n, let E_n be the set of triples (S,T,U) with S ⊂ T ⊂ U in B_n such that |S| + |T| = |U|. The conjecture states that |E_n| = C(2n,n) - [x^n](1+x+x^2)^n - 2^n + 1, where [x^n] extracts the coefficient of x^n from the polynomial. This identity connects poset chain counting in Boolean lattices with trinomial coefficient extraction and binomial sums, and is the foundational combinatorial identity underlying the paper's analysis of multiplicity parameters.
proof_strategy: The proof proceeds by classifying triples (S,T,U) with S ⊂ T ⊂ U in B_n according to the rank levels of S, T, U (i.e., their cardinalities). The condition |S|+|T| = |U| constrains the rank levels. One sums over all valid rank triples (i,j,i+j) with i < j < i+j ≤ n, counting the number of ways to choose nested subsets at those ranks via inclusion (choosing U\T, T\S, and S independently from appropriate ground sets). The trinomial coefficient [x^n](1+x+x^2)^n arises as the count of triples where the chain condition S ⊂ T ⊂ U is violated (i.e., where some inclusions are not strict), and the term 2^n - 1 accounts for degenerate cases. The identity follows from inclusion-exclusion over these cases.
title: Exact enumeration of arithmetic Schur-type triples in the Boolean lattice

description: For every fixed graph H that contains at least one edge, the decision problem Chromatic Sum remains NP‑complete when restricted to H‑free graphs (i.e., graphs that do not contain H as a subgraph). This conjecture is falsifiable because a single counterexample—a graph class H‑free for which Chromatic Sum is polynomial‑time solvable— would refute it.
proof_strategy: Establish NP‑membership in NP and prove NP‑hardness via a reduction from a known NP‑complete problem (e.g., 3‑Partition) while respecting the H‑free restriction.
title: Chromatic Sum is NP-complete on H‑free graphs for any fixed graph H with at least one edge

description: For n ≥ 2, any 1-intersecting family F ⊆ S_n (i.e., any two permutations in F agree on at least one point) satisfies |F| ≤ (n−1)!. Equality holds if and only if F is a dictatorship {σ ∈ S_n : σ(i) = j} for some i, j. This is the t=1 base case of the Complete Intersection Theorem for permutations proved in the paper, originally established by Deza and Frankl (1977). Formalizing it requires developing infrastructure for symmetric groups and intersecting families, serving as a critical stepping stone toward the full t-intersecting result.
proof_strategy: Follow the representation-theoretic approach: the permutation module M^{i→j} of S_n acting on [n] has irreducible decomposition enabling eigenvalue bounds on independent sets in the derangement graph. The derangement graph on S_n is a Cayley graph whose largest eigenvalue gives the (n−1)! bound via the Hoffman bound / Delsarte-Hoffman inequality, and the equality case is characterized by analyzing eigenspaces. Alternatively, use the spread approximation method from Kupavskii-Zakharov as refined in the paper, which avoids heavy representation theory.
title: Deza-Frankl Theorem: Maximum 1-Intersecting Families in S_n are Dictatorships

description: For any primitive holomorphic cusp form f of even weight k ≥ 2 for Γ₀(N), at least 1/3 of the zeros of the family of twisted L-functions L(s, f × χ) lie on the critical line Re(s) = 1/2, where χ ranges over primitive Dirichlet characters of conductor ≤ Q as Q → ∞. This extends the paper's positive-proportion result for PGL(2) (which likely yields ~1/9 via Levinson's method with current mollifier lengths) to the expected optimal proportion, analogous to Levinson's classical 1/3 result for the Riemann zeta function. The proportion is defined as liminf_{Q→∞} N_{crit}(f, Q) / N_{total}(f, Q) where N_{crit} counts zeros on Re(s)=1/2 and N_{total} counts zeros in the critical strip across the family.
proof_strategy: Adapt Levinson's zero-detection method with optimized multi-parameter mollifiers for the family L(s, f × χ), leveraging the paper's asymptotic large sieve with power-saving error terms for PGL(2) twisted L-functions. The key bottleneck is constructing mollifiers of sufficient length—current techniques using the paper's mean value theorem with θ=0 error term O(Q^{7/4+ε}) yield a smaller proportion. Achieving 1/3 requires either: (1) extending the allowable mollifier length θ beyond 1/2−ε in the mean value theorem, or (2) developing a twisted analogue of Conrey's refinements to Levinson's method, using the extra averaging over χ to absorb longer mollifiers. The unconditional nature of the PGL(2) results (no GRC needed) makes this approach viable.
title: One-Third Proportion Conjecture for Critical Zeros of GL(2) Twisted L-functions

description: Conjecture: Any arithmetic function f : ℕ → ℂ with |f(n)| ≤ 1 for all n, satisfying a completed L-function functional equation Λ_f(s)=ε Λ_f(1-s) for some root of unity ε, and assuming that the minimal conductor N>1 is such that the support of f is contained in {1,…,N}, must be a primitive Dirichlet character modulo N. In particular f must be completely multiplicative, have absolute value 1 on coprime arguments, and its order must divide the parity of ε.
proof_strategy: Apply Mellin transform techniques to the Dirichlet series ∑ f(n)/n^s to derive analytic continuation and functional equation constraints; then use Fourier analysis on finite abelian groups to show that boundedness and the functional equation force multiplicativity and character-like behaviour.
title: Functional Equations Characterize Primitive Dirichlet Characters

description: A connected reductive group G over an algebraically closed field k of characteristic p > 0 admits a Springer isomorphism (a G-equivariant isomorphism between the unipotent variety and the nilpotent cone) if and only if for every unipotent element u in G(k), the centralizer Z_G(u) is smooth. The paper establishes that PGL_p in characteristic p has non-smooth unipotent centralizers and no Springer isomorphism; this conjecture posits these two phenomena are equivalent in general.
proof_strategy: The 'only if' direction: show that a Springer isomorphism maps each unipotent centralizer isomorphically onto the corresponding nilpotent stabilizer, and nilpotent stabilizers are always smooth for reductive groups in good characteristic. The 'if' direction: use the smoothness of all unipotent centralizers to construct the isomorphism via the Dynkin-Spaltenstein construction, ensuring the scheme-theoretic conditions are satisfied. Lean formalization would require developing the theory of unipotent varieties, nilpotent cones, G-equivariant morphisms of schemes, and smoothness criteria for group scheme centralizers.
title: Springer Isomorphism Characterization via Centralizer Smoothness

description: For every pair of increasing (monotone) Boolean functions f, g : {0,1}^n → {0,1} equipped with the uniform measure, the covariance satisfies Cov(f,g) ≥ 4 · ∑_{∅≠S⊆[n]} |S| · f̂(S)² · ĝ(S)², where f̂(S) denotes the Fourier-Walsh coefficient of f at character χ_S. This is a sharp Fourier-analytic strengthening of the Harris–Kleitman inequality, with optimal constant 4 and complete equality characterization.
proof_strategy: The original proof uses a correlated four-restriction induction coupling the four codimension-one restricted pairs with correlation 1/2, extracting degree-weighted diagonal spectral energy as a nonnegative square, plus a sharp endpoint convolution inequality. Formalization should proceed in layers: (1) build Fourier-Walsh analysis on the discrete cube with uniform measure, including Plancherel and convolution identities; (2) prove the four-restriction identity linking Cov(f,g) to restricted covariances with the 1/2 correlation coupling; (3) establish the endpoint convolution inequality; (4) assemble via induction on dimension. The equality characterization (dictatorships and the AND-OR pair up to relabelling) could be a separate milestone.
title: Sharp Diagonal Spectral Correlation Inequality for Increasing Boolean Functions

description: For any integers 2 ≤ s < t and any n-vertex graph G, the t-clique density of G is bounded below by the composition of the Lovász-Simonovits t-clique density function evaluated at the generalized inverse of the s-clique density function applied to the s-clique density of G. Specifically, k_t(G) / n^t ≥ F_t(F_s^{-1}(k_s(G) / n^s)). This encompasses Reiher's clique density theorem as a special case when s=2.
proof_strategy: First, formalize Turán graphs and compute their s-clique and r-clique counts to establish the critical points. Define the piecewise linear function L_{s,r} and prove Bollobás's original piecewise-linear interpolation bound. Define the Lovász-Simonovits clique density function F_r and its generalized inverse F_s^{-1}. Finally, formalize the inductive proof strategy presented in the paper, showing that the piecewise-linear bound is superseded by the continuous bound involving F_t and F_s^{-1}.
title: Asymptotic Clique-to-Clique Density Bound

description: The main result establishing the exact exponential growth rate of the ρ-th moment of constrained guesswork G_coset for a random binary linear code of rate R under i.i.d. Bernoulli(p) noise. It demonstrates that the exponent shifts down by exactly ρ(1-R) relative to the unconstrained Arıkan--Merhav exponent, yielding a closed-form limit expressed in terms of the binary Rényi entropy.
proof_strategy: Define the probability space for random binary linear codes and the constrained guesswork rank. Prove the universality theorem, expressing the guesswork exponent as a functional of the weight-enumerator growth rate: (1+ρ)ψ_{1/(1+ρ)}(g) - ρψ_1(g). Then, evaluate this Legendre-type transform for the specific weight-enumerator growth rate of random linear codes to derive the closed-form exponent ρ h_{1/(1+ρ)}(p) + ρ(R-1).
title: Exact Exponent for Constrained Coset Guesswork

description: This paper investigates the enumeration and structural properties of so-called deranged unit-interval parking functions, linking their count to deranged Bell numbers and introducing a characterization via block indices and displacement constraints. It aims to provide a precise formula for their size using combinatorial methods and symbolic computation.
proof_strategy: symbolic derivation + asymptotic refinement
title: Deranged unit-interval parking functions and their combinatorial enumeration

description: Given a finite, strongly connected, edge-weighted digraph G and a color equivalence relation ≡ on the formal convex combinations of vertices (an equivalence relation respecting convex combination: px + (1-p)y ≡ z ⟹ q(px+(1-p)y) + (1-q)w ≡ qz + (1-q)w), if every vertex v is equivalent (under ≡) to the weighted blend of its out-neighbors, then all vertices are pairwise equivalent. This generalizes the classical harmonic lemma from real-valued functions to arbitrary color-blending operations, and is the main theorem of the paper.
proof_strategy: Formalize formal convex combinations over a finite type, color equivalence relations (equivalence relations on convex combos satisfying the congruence property), and strongly connected edge-weighted digraphs. Reproduce the Markov chain stopping rule argument: define a random walk on the digraph, show that under the harmonic hypothesis the color at any starting vertex equals the expected color at a stopping time, and use strong connectivity plus finiteness to argue all vertex colors must be equivalent. The key inductive step uses the color equivalence axiom to push the blend through each step of the walk.
title: Chromonic Lemma: No Nontrivial Harmonic Colorings Exist on Strongly Connected Digraphs

description: Let F be a CM number field, n ≥ 2, and ℓ a rational prime. Let ρ̄ : G_F → GL_n(F̄_ℓ) be a continuous irreducible representation arising from the mod ℓ Betti cohomology of the locally symmetric space for GL_n/F. Then for every finite place v | ℓ of F, the restriction ρ̄|_{G_{F_v}} is de Rham, and its Hodge–Tate weights are determined by the infinitesimal character of the corresponding local component π_v of the automorphic representation associated to ρ̄. This extends the paper's local-global compatibility at v ∤ ℓ to the much deeper v | ℓ case.
proof_strategy: Combine p-adic deformation theory of Galois representations with mod ℓ local Langlands correspondences. Key steps: (1) Establish that torsion Galois representations from Betti cohomology admit integral p-adic lifts to characteristic zero via patching arguments generalizing the Taylor–Wiles method. (2) Prove these lifts are geometric (de Rham) at v | ℓ by relating their filtered (φ, N)-modules to the Breuil–Mézard compatibilities for the mod ℓ representation. (3) Match Hodge–Tate weights with the infinitesimal character using the compatibility of the group determinant at v | ℓ, extending Scholze's construction via perfectoid Shimura varieties and the Hodge–Tate period map.
title: De Rham Local-Global Compatibility for Torsion Automorphic Forms on GL_n over CM Fields

description: For any integer $g \ge 2$, let $d \in \{2g+1, 2g+2\}$, $\alpha \in \mathbb{Z} \setminus \{0\}$, and let $p$ be a prime such that $p > P^+(d)$ and $p \nmid \alpha$, where $P^+(d)$ is the bound from the paper ($d^2-4d+2$ if $d$ is odd, $(d^2-3d+2)/2$ if $d$ is even). Let $M(t)$ be the $g \times g$ Cartier-Manin matrix of the hyperelliptic curve $y^2 = x^d + \alpha x + t$ over $\mathbb{F}_p$. The determinant $\det(M(t))$ is a nonzero polynomial in $\mathbb{F}_p[t]$.
proof_strategy: Define the Cartier-Manin matrix entries as coefficients of the polynomial $(x^d + \alpha x + t)^{(p-1)/2}$, compute its determinant as a polynomial in $t$, and show that its degree and leading coefficient modulo $p$ imply nonvanishing, leveraging the bounds on $p$-adic valuations of the terms which hold precisely when $p > P^+(d)$ and $p \nmid \alpha$.
title: Nonvanishing of Cartier-Manin Determinant for Generic Hyperelliptic Families

description: Let π̂(x) denote the incremental prime-counting estimator constructed from the generalized triangular number partition of [2, x] augmented with the proposed correction term. The conjecture states that π̂(x) ∼ li(x) as x → ∞, i.e., lim_{x→∞} π̂(x) / li(x) = 1, and more precisely that |π̂(x) − π(x)| = O(√x · log x). This would formalize the empirical observation that the corrected estimator achieves accuracy comparable to classical analytic approximations while retaining its O(√x) computational structure.
proof_strategy: First, formalize the generalized triangular number partition and the discrete sum approximating li(x) in Lean. Prove that the uncorrected Riemann-sum estimator converges to li(x) by bounding the discretization error of the non-uniform quadrature against the continuous integral definition of li(x). Then, show the correction term is o(li(x)), which would establish π̂(x) ∼ li(x) by the Prime Number Theorem. The O(√x · log x) error bound would require analyzing how the partition mesh size √x and the correction term interact, likely using partial summation and bounds on the density of primes in short intervals.
title: Corrected Triangular-Partition Estimator Asymptotically Matches the Logarithmic Integral

description: For pro-p groups A and B, the F_p-cup radical of their free pro-p product decomposes as R_p(A *_p B) ≅ R_p(A) ⊕ R_p(B), under the natural Mayer-Vietoris identification H^1(A *_p B, F_p) ≅ H^1(A, F_p) ⊕ H^1(B, F_p). Equivalently, R_p(A *_p B) = res_A^{-1}(R_p(A)) ∩ res_B^{-1}(R_p(B)), where res_A and res_B are the restriction maps. This captures the stability of the cup radical under free pro-p products, a key structural result underlying the paper's proof that the p-Kijima-Nishi property is preserved under free pro-p product constructions.
proof_strategy: Use the Mayer-Vietoris long exact sequence for free pro-p products to identify H^1(A *_p B, F_p) ≅ H^1(A, F_p) ⊕ H^1(B, F_p) and H^2(A *_p B, F_p) ≅ H^2(A, F_p) ⊕ H^2(B, F_p). Show that under these decompositions, the cup product on H^1(A *_p B) decomposes componentwise: (α_A, α_B) ⌣ (β_A, β_B) = (α_A ⌣ β_A, α_B ⌣ β_B). Then an element (α_A, α_B) lies in R_p(A *_p B) iff α_A ⌣ β_A = 0 for all β_A and α_B ⌣ β_B = 0 for all β_B, i.e., iff α_A ∈ R_p(A) and α_B ∈ R_p(B).
title: Cup Radical Decomposition for Free Pro-p Products

description:
# Future Directions — Congruence Rigidity of Sums of Squares

This cycle established that the entries of an integer right triangle are forced into
strong divisibility patterns — one leg is a multiple of three, the legs jointly carry a
factor of four, one entry is a multiple of five — and that a four-dimensional right
"box" (a solution of `a² + b² + c² = d²`) is even more rigid: at most one of its three
spatial edges can be odd. We also pinned down exactly which whole numbers can serve as a
leg. These findings point to several bold, testable conjectures.

## 1. The correct modulus for a power of two grows with the power
**Conjecture.** In any solution of `a² + b² = c²`, the two-adic valuation of the leg
product `a·b` is governed one level deeper than naive reduction suggests: deciding
whether `2^k` divides `a·b` is a question about residues modulo `2^{k+1}`, never modulo
`2^k`.
*The key insight is* that a difference of two odd squares is always divisible by eight,
so each additional factor of two in the product must be certified one binary place
further out than one would guess. *Why now?* Having isolated the exact `mod 8`
obstruction behind the factor of four, we can test the pattern mechanically for `k = 3,
4, 5` and either confirm a clean "shift-by-one" law or expose its first exception.

## 2. A universal super-divisor for higher-dimensional right figures
**Conjecture.** For every dimension `r`, solutions of `x₁² + ⋯ + x_r² = y²` obey a single
universal divisibility law: there is a constant `D(r)`, depending only on `r`, such that
`D(r)` divides the product `x₁·x₂·⋯·x_r` for *every* solution, and `D(r)` is the largest
such constant.
*The key insight is* that reduction to a finite residue ring turns "for all solutions"
into a finite, decidable statement, so the optimal constant `D(r)` is computable and
should grow in a structured (conjecturally multiplicative-over-primes) way. *Why now?*
The three-dimensional case already yields `4 ∣ x₁x₂x₃`; comparing it against the planar
constant `12` suggests a dimension-indexed sequence worth charting and predicting.

## 3. Parity collapse in higher dimensions
**Conjecture.** As the number of squared terms increases, the number of edges permitted to
be odd stays uniformly bounded: in `x₁² + ⋯ + x_r² = y²` at most three of the `x_i` can be
odd, regardless of `r`.
*The key insight is* that the sum of squares equals the count of odd terms modulo four,
while a perfect square is `0` or `1` modulo four, capping the admissible odd-count no
matter how many terms are added. *Why now?* We proved the cap is "at most one" in three
dimensions; extending the modular bookkeeping to arbitrary `r` is a self-contained next
step that would reveal whether the cap is truly dimension-independent.

## 4. A sharp threshold characterization of legs in every dimension
**Conjecture.** Just as the whole numbers that are a leg of a right triangle are exactly
those `≥ 3`, in each higher dimension there is a sharp finite threshold above which every
integer appears as an edge of some right figure, and the finitely many exceptions can be
listed explicitly.
*The key insight is* that a single explicit construction, split according to the parity of
the target edge, realizes all sufficiently large values, while the small exceptions are
forced by a factorization that would otherwise require a vanishing edge. *Why now?* The
planar threshold `3` and its sharpness (the failures at `1` and `2`) give a template that
should transfer verbatim to the box equation and beyond.

## 5. Divisibility as a sieve against near-solutions
**Conjecture.** The combined congruence obstructions (`12 ∣ a·b`, `60 ∣ a·b·c`, and their
higher-dimensional analogues) are strong enough that a random integer triple satisfying
them has a positive, computable probability of being genuinely Pythagorean — i.e. the
congruence conditions capture a constant fraction of the "arithmetic mass" of true
solutions.
*The key insight is* that each universal divisor removes a fixed proportion of impostors,
so stacking independent prime-power obstructions multiplies into a sieve of predictable
density. *Why now?* With the exact obstructions in hand for the primes `2, 3, 5`, one can
immediately measure how much of the solution set they explain and calibrate whether a few
